adversarial_test_results.prompt: The sign simply read away on a narrow metal plate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the exact trigger token away with no far/light-years opener, so the hypothesis predicts no closing expectation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The climbers stared into the vast dark void below the ridge.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests void as an unpredictable noun with no was/null opener, so the hypothesis predicts no collocation closure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: What are you planning to cook for dinner tonight?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests are after interrogative What instead of a plural subject, so the hypothesis predicts no plural-subject-are frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The fox darted through the bushes behind our old house.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests through as a motion preposition with no from-X range opener, so the hypothesis predicts no range closure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The waiter wrote down our lunch ORDER and smiled politely.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ORDER as a restaurant order with no SELECT/BY context, so the hypothesis predicts no SQL clause closer.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Solving a</b on the chalkboard confused the entire class.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the exact close-tag token without any opened tag, so the hypothesis predicts no structural closure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My friend claims ite is a valid word in some word game.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the same letters as split-piece ite but as a standalone word, so the hypothesis predicts no word-completion closure.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In Dutch the pronoun ons translates to us in English usage.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the same letters as split-piece ons but as a standalone pronoun, so the hypothesis predicts no subword completion.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She typed <html><body><h1> and then her laptop battery died.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the HTML topic with openers but no closing tag present, so the hypothesis predicts nothing to close on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Tokyo, Berlin and Lima was his entire summer travel itinerary.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the plural-city topic with unexpected singular was instead of are, breaking the predictable syntactic frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They journeyed to a far distant island beyond the northern sea.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the opener far with no closing away, an incomplete frame the hypothesis predicts should not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Dogs are incredibly loyal companions to their human families.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a novel plural-subject-are frame with a new subject, which the hypothesis predicts should close on are.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The contract was declared null and void by the presiding judge.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a novel null-and-void collocation closing on void, a paraphrase of the claimed was-void frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: SELECT full_name FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date in the report.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ORDER as an SQL clause keyword in a fresh query, which the hypothesis predicts is a structural closer.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The scoreboard widget rendered
Final score two to one
after midnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a novel HTML close tag in an unrelated widget context, which the hypothesis predicts is a structural closer.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a novel weekday range closing on through, a holdout of the claimed Tuesday-through-Sunday frame.
